name: State Bank of India
summary: State Bank of India recruits Probationary Officers and Junior Associates (clerks) through public exams announced in official notifications on its careers page. Recent officer notifications describe a preliminary exam, a main exam, then a psychometric test, a group exercise and an interview; clerk recruitment is mainly through preliminary and main exams, with a local-language test for some candidates. Specialist Cadre Officer roles, such as IT, risk and law, are advertised separately.
rounds: Online application against an official notification on SBI's careers page
Phase I: an online preliminary exam (objective), used to shortlist for the main exam
Phase II: an online main exam; for officers it usually includes objective and descriptive tests
Officers, Phase III: usually a psychometric test, a group exercise and a personal interview
Clerks: a test of the chosen local language for candidates who didn't study it at school, as the notification sets out
Document verification and a medical check before joining
Specialist Cadre Officers: separate notifications by post; selection varies, often shortlisting and an interview
looks_for: In the interview: clear communication, awareness of banking and the economy, and a sound reason for choosing SBI
In the group exercise: contributing ideas, listening and helping the group reach a conclusion
Willingness to work in any branch, including rural and semi-urban ones

questions.text: Tell me about a time you helped someone who was unfamiliar with a process, such as filling in a form or using an app.
covers: Who they were and what they found hard
How you explained it patiently, in their language and at their pace
What they could do afterwards on their own

questions.text: Describe a time you led a group without being formally in charge.
covers: The group's goal and why someone needed to step up
What you did to organise people and settle disagreements
The result and what the others would say about your role

questions.text: Tell me about a time you stayed polite with someone who was being rude or unreasonable.
covers: What happened and why they were upset
How you kept calm and still solved the problem
How it ended, and what you'd do the same way again

questions.text: Tell me about a time you chose honesty even though it was the harder option.
covers: The situation and the easier, less honest option
What you did and who you told
What it cost or gained you, and why you'd do it again

questions.text: What is financial inclusion, and how does a bank like SBI support it?
covers: Access to basic accounts, credit, insurance and pensions for people who lack them
Government schemes, business correspondents and digital banking as ways to reach them
The challenges that remain, and what a branch officer can do

questions.text: Explain the repo rate and the cash reserve ratio, and how changes in them affect lending.
covers: Repo rate: what the RBI charges banks to borrow; CRR: the share of deposits banks must keep with the RBI
A higher repo rate or CRR usually makes loans dearer or reduces money to lend
Why the RBI uses them: inflation and growth

questions.text: A farmer in your branch area is struggling to repay a crop loan after a poor monsoon. What would you consider?
covers: Understanding the situation: crop loss, other income, the loan's history
Options within the rules, such as restructuring, crop insurance claims or relief schemes
Being fair to the farmer and to the bank, and documenting the decision

questions.text: How would you increase the use of digital banking among older customers at a rural branch?
covers: The barriers: trust, language, phones and fear of fraud
Practical steps: assisted demonstrations, local-language help, safety tips
How you'd measure progress and keep a branch option for those who need it

questions.text: A customer says they shared an OTP on a phone call and money has left their account. What would you do?
covers: Blocking the card or account access and recording the complaint at once
Guiding them to report it through the bank's process and the national cybercrime helpline
Explaining next steps calmly, and how to spot such calls in future

questions.text: What is a non-performing asset, and why does it matter to a public-sector bank?
covers: A loan overdue beyond the RBI's limit, usually 90 days
Its effect on profits, capital and the bank's ability to lend
How banks reduce it: careful lending, monitoring and recovery

questions.text: Group exercise practice: should India move towards a fully cashless economy? Give your view and a counterpoint.
covers: A clear position with two reasons
A fair counterpoint: access, connectivity, fraud, the informal economy
How you would help the group reach a shared conclusion

questions.text: Explain one recent RBI or government step in banking and what it means for ordinary customers.
covers: The step, described accurately and briefly
Who it affects and how
One benefit and one challenge in putting it into practice

questions.text: Tell me about yourself and why you want to join SBI.
covers: Your background in a few sentences: home town, education, any work
What draws you to SBI and to banking
A quality that would make you a good officer or associate

questions.text: Why a public-sector bank rather than a private bank?
covers: Reasons about the work: reach, public service, variety of postings
Something specific about SBI
A respectful answer that doesn't criticise private banks

questions.text: You may be posted to a remote rural branch far from home. How do you feel about that?
covers: An honest, positive answer
What you'd learn there that a city branch wouldn't teach
How you would adapt: language, community, living arrangements

tips: Read the official notification for your cycle on SBI's careers page: stages, eligibility and dates change, and the notification is the authority.
SBI says it informs shortlisted candidates individually and publishes only roll or registration numbers; ignore any message asking for money.
For the interview, prepare to talk about your own background (home district, degree subjects, hobbies), as panels often start there.
In the group exercise, make a clear point early, build on others' points, help the group summarise, and don't talk over people.
Know SBI's core values (Service, Transparency, Ethics, Politeness, Sustainability) and have one example for each from your life.
Follow banking and economy news daily: RBI policy, government schemes, digital payments and financial inclusion.
